summary: HELLO-MARS helps rovers survive on Mars by finding the safest, fastest, and lowest-energy costing routes. Team KYRONIX - NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
details: HELLO-MARS is an Interplanetary Survival Guide for Mars rovers. The user opens an interactive Mars map, chooses a Start point and an Arrival point, and marks dangers like craters, rocks, and steep slopes in red. When the user clicks CALCULATE, our algorithm instantly calculates and compares 4 different routes. It shows them on the map in different colors with their Safety Score, Travel Time, and Energy Use.It prevents rovers from driving into dangerous terrain. It saves mission time by choosing the fastest safe route. It saves battery by choosing the lowest-energy route. Mission teams can test many routes in seconds, without risking a real $2.5 billion rover.it's intended to make future Mars missions safer and longer. If a rover avoids just one crater, it can survive months longer and send back more science. Our tool can be used for real Mars missions, for Moon missions, and even for rescue robots on Earth in disaster zones.We used Python with Flask for the backend, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the interactive map, and a pathfinding algorithm to calculate the best routes. We used NASA Mars terrain data as inspiration for the hazards, and Render to host the live website. We used Clipchamp to record our demo video.Instead of just showing a map, we turned it into a Survival Guide. We don't give just ONE route, we give 4 choices - Sentinel, Discovery, Fortress and Sprint - so the astronaut can decide what matters most for that mission. We use simple colors and scores so anyone can understand it in 10 seconds.We considered 3 main factors: 1) Safety - avoid craters, rocks and slopes. 2) Time - a shorter route means more science done. 3) Energy - Mars rovers run on solar power, so saving battery is saving life. We also considered that the interface must be simple enough for a non-expert to use in an emergency.
